title: Almond and cherry cookies
subtitle: soft, golden cookies with ground almonds and tart dried cherries
excerpt: Almond and cherry cookies are soft, thick cookies made with ground almonds in the dough for a chewy, slightly dense crumb and tart dried cherries folded through for contrast. They are scooped and baked without chilling, giving a thick, domed shape. The almond extract in the dough reinforces the almond flavour alongside the ground almonds.
sourceNotes: Almond-based drop cookies have a long tradition in Italian baking, particularly the amaretti, which uses ground almonds and egg whites. The combination with dried cherries reflects a broader American and British home-baking tradition of mixing dried fruit into drop cookie doughs.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the baked cookies in a single layer, then transfer to a container for up to 2 months. Thaw at room temperature for 30 minutes.
recipe.batchNotes: The dough doubles well. Bake in batches.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Keeps at room temperature in an airtight tin for up to 5 days.

content.text: Almond and cherry cookies are soft drop cookies made with both ground almonds and plain flour. The ground almonds give the finished cookie a denser, chewier crumb than a flour-only biscuit. Dried cherries add bursts of tartness through the dough. The dough does not need chilling and can go straight onto the tray; the cookies hold their shape well and come out thick and domed.
Heat the oven to 175 degrees C (fan 155 degrees C / gas 3 to 4). Line baking trays with baking paper.
Beat the softened butter and caster sugar together until light and creamy, about 3 minutes. Beat in the egg and almond extract.
Stir in the flour, ground almonds, baking powder, and salt until combined. Fold in the dried cherries.
Scoop tablespoons of dough onto the trays, spaced 5 cm apart. Press a pinch of flaked almonds onto each cookie if using.
Bake for 11 to 13 minutes until the edges are lightly golden and the centres are set but still look slightly soft. Leave on the tray for 5 minutes before moving to a cooling rack.

attrs.problem: Cookies very pale and soft rather than golden
attrs.avoid: Avoid undershooting the oven temperature; the ground almonds in the dough mean the cookies look lighter than a flour-only biscuit even when done.
attrs.fix: Check at 11 minutes and look for a definite golden edge rather than overall colour. The centres will firm up fully as the cookies cool.

attrs.problem: Dried cherries sinking to the bottom during baking
attrs.avoid: Avoid adding cherries that are very heavy or coated in excess syrup.
attrs.fix: Toss the dried cherries lightly in a teaspoon of the measured flour before folding in. This helps them stay suspended through the dough.
